question: Does the slot trainer restore its optimizer, schedule, cursor and random streams so that subsequent GPU updates agree; do briefly updated weights retain numerical validity?
hypothesis: The existing atomic save/resume helpers restore all state used by these models. Initialization-only numerical checks are insufficient evidence about updated weights.

sources.sections: Saving and Loading a General Checkpoint; Saving and Loading Models Across Devices
sources.consequence: Exercise actual model and Adam state restoration, with a new model/optimizer and explicit train/eval mode. Loading weights alone is insufficient.

sources.sections: Reproducibility, controlling sources of randomness, convolution benchmarking and deterministic algorithms
sources.consequence: Test CPU and GPU RNG draws exactly in the same environment, and separately test step-keyed local generators. Do not infer cross-platform bitwise reproducibility.

sources.sections: Floating-point accuracy, batched and slice computations, nonfinite values
sources.consequence: Use declared numerical tolerances for outputs, gradients and optimizer updates; report repeat/batch regrouping separately from resumed-state agreement.

sources.sections: save, resume, generator, train_stage loss/checkpoint/optimizer sequence
sources.consequence: Use the actual save/resume/generator helpers and model losses. Keep epoch-loss accumulator, best score and next-batch cursor in the roundtrip.

differences: A small synthetic-input implementation diagnostic, not a balls learning result or an end-to-end full trainer test. Default n3 models, batch two; RGB clips have three frames rather than six. A six-step warmup/cosine schedule compresses the slot schedule to exercise LR changes in three updates. CPU work is forward/backward comparison only; every optimizer update runs on the dedicated GPU. Original trainers and their source are untouched.
contrary_evidence: RNG restoration alone cannot eliminate nondeterministic kernels; a short same-process checkpoint roundtrip does not establish crash recovery at every trainer boundary or long-horizon learning stability. Passing synthetic updated-weight checks does not validate final trained checkpoints.

protocol.optimizer: Adam, RGB lr=1e-4 clip=0.05; predictor lr=5e-4 no clipping
protocol.schedule: RGB warmup two steps then cosine to step six; predictor constant
protocol.resume: Save with actual trainer save, continue two updates, instantiate fresh model/Adam/scheduler, restore with actual resume and repeat those updates. Compare every model/optimizer tensor, scheduler scalar, saved cursor/best/epoch-loss fields, next CPU/GPU RNG draws and per-step losses. Assert checkpoint bytes are unchanged by loading.
protocol.rng: Global CPU/GPU random draws and actual independently seeded step-keyed slot/mask generators; no Python/NumPy random input pipeline in this diagnostic
protocol.numerics: After three updates: eval CPU/GPU outputs and every trainable parameter gradient, including RGB decoder reconstruction/masks; GPU batched, separate-item, reversed-batch and repeat outputs. Report finite values and missing-gradient names explicitly.
checks: nested tensor/state comparison rejects a changed optimizer tensor
RNG equality rejects a changed draw

success: Both models pass the scoped resume and updated-weight numerical checks. This authorizes only the already-preregistered C001 implementation validity claim; final learned-model performance remains unmeasured.
stop: Preserve any failure and consult literature before changing numerical policy or implementing a fix. No full training, no model hyperparameter changes, no selection on synthetic diagnostic performance. Stop at the shared or local time limit.

resources.allocation: existing validation reserve within the shared 48 hours
resources.concurrency: small diagnostic may coexist with original six trainers
